Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 0.4770 | ≤ EUR 0.4739 | ≥ EUR 0.4878 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 37.69 | ≤ EUR 0.4741 | ≥ EUR 0.5003 | HOLD |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.784 | ≤ EUR 0.4751 | ≥ EUR 0.4771 | HOLD |
| MACD crossover | MACD = -0.0032<br>Signal = -0.0029<br>Gap = -0.0003<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 0.4813 | — | — | SELL |
| Consensus | BUY 0/4; SELL 1/4; neutral 3/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

![VLP1L Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/VLP1L_technicals_6m.png?v=2fbb09e1a2c8)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 15.7500 | ≤ EUR 15.1457 | ≥ EUR 16.0093 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 58.83 | ≤ EUR 14.7757 | ≥ EUR 15.9943 | HOLD |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.097 | ≤ EUR 15.7836 | ≥ EUR 16.0940 | BUY |
| MACD crossover | MACD = 0.1167<br>Signal = 0.1021<br>Gap = +0.0146<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 15.5207 | — | — | BUY |
| Consensus | BUY 2/4; SELL 0/4; neutral 2/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

![MRK1T Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/MRK1T_technicals_6m.png?v=87cd409e355d)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 26.9000 | ≤ EUR 26.8866 | ≥ EUR 27.1784 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 40.95 | ≤ EUR 26.6911 | ≥ EUR 27.6306 | HOLD |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.292 | ≤ EUR 26.8834 | ≥ EUR 27.0060 | HOLD |
| MACD crossover | MACD = -0.0427<br>Signal = -0.0242<br>Gap = -0.0185<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 27.1895 | — | — | SELL |
| Consensus | BUY 0/4; SELL 1/4; neutral 3/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

The selected share is highlighted, while every other eligible Baltic share is shown as an unlabelled transparent background point. The horizontal coordinate is the realised mean one-period return. The vertical coordinate is the five-year average annual historical dividend yield: each ex-dividend amount is divided by the latest available share price on or before that ex-dividend date, annual event yields are summed, and the five calendar years 2022–2026 are averaged including zero-payment years. ![MOLNR Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/MOLNR_technicals_6m.png?v=ed3983454b25)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 19.8000 | ≤ EUR 19.4639 | ≥ EUR 21.9361 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 46.23 | ≤ EUR 17.1493 | ≥ EUR 23.6812 | HOLD |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.000 | ≤ EUR 20.0505 | ≥ EUR 20.9838 | BUY |
| MACD crossover | MACD = 0.1695<br>Signal = 0.3981<br>Gap = -0.2286<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 23.3823 | — | — | SELL |
| Consensus | BUY 1/4; SELL 1/4; neutral 2/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

<summary>Profit outcome and subsequent price analysis (3 classified of 10 earnings releases)</summary>

Higher/lower profit refers to the issuer's explicit comparison with the earlier comparable period. ‘In line / unchanged’ is used only when the issuer explicitly says that profit met a plan, forecast or expectation, or was unchanged. ‘Loss’ requires an explicit realised net or operating loss. Releases without such wording remain unclassified and are excluded from the conditional estimates.

Variance is reported in squared percentage points. Abnormal return is the share return minus the equal-weight Baltic-market return over the same horizon.

**Kruskal–Wallis test across the available outcome groups**

At least two outcome groups with two observations each are required; this share does not have enough observations for the omnibus test.

**Pairwise result:** No pairwise difference survives BH adjustment.

The test describes historical association. Small groups, overlapping horizons and repeated releases from the same company limit causal interpretation.

The selected share is highlighted, while every other eligible Baltic share is shown as an unlabelled transparent background point. The horizontal coordinate is the realised mean one-period return. The vertical coordinate is the five-year average annual historical dividend yield: each ex-dividend amount is divided by the latest available share price on or before that ex-dividend date, annual event yields are summed, and the five calendar years 2022–2026 are averaged including zero-payment years. Portfolio values are weight-averaged constituent yields. This is descriptive and is not a dividend forecast.

![RSU1L Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/RSU1L_technicals_6m.png?v=7d5e9fe0c2e4)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 4.2600 | ≤ EUR 4.3021 | ≥ EUR 4.5619 | BUY |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 22.59 | ≤ EUR 4.3406 | ≥ EUR 4.6734 | BUY |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.000 | ≤ EUR 4.3315 | ≥ EUR 4.3968 | BUY |
| MACD crossover | MACD = -0.0454<br>Signal = -0.0269<br>Gap = -0.0185<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 4.5506 | — | — | SELL |
| Consensus | BUY 3/4; SELL 1/4; neutral 0/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | BUY |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

At least two outcome groups with two observations each are required; this share does not have enough observations for the omnibus test.

The test describes historical association. Small groups, overlapping horizons and repeated releases from the same company limit causal interpretation.

![RSU1L mean return and historical dividend yield with all portfolios](figures/return_dividend_all_portfolios.png?v=9b46f9677dcd)

The selected share is highlighted, while every other eligible Baltic share is shown as an unlabelled transparent background point. The horizontal coordinate is the realised mean one-period return. The vertical coordinate is the five-year average annual historical dividend yield: each ex-dividend amount is divided by the latest available share price on or before that ex-dividend date, annual event yields are summed, and the five calendar years 2022–2026 are averaged including zero-payment years. Portfolio values are weight-averaged constituent yields. This is descriptive and is not a dividend forecast.

![APG1L Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/APG1L_technicals_6m.png?v=42cb34d090f6)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 3.8000 | ≤ EUR 3.7732 | ≥ EUR 3.8508 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 39.77 | ≤ EUR 3.7786 | ≥ EUR 3.9487 | HOLD |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.973 | ≤ EUR 3.7837 | ≥ EUR 3.7960 | SELL |
| MACD crossover | MACD = -0.0245<br>Signal = -0.0264<br>Gap = +0.0019<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 3.7704 | — | — | BUY |
| Consensus | BUY 1/4; SELL 1/4; neutral 2/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

<details markdown="1" class="earnings-outcomes">
<summary>Profit outcome and subsequent price analysis (7 classified of 13 earnings releases)</summary>

Higher/lower profit refers to the issuer's explicit comparison with the earlier comparable period. ‘In line / unchanged’ is used only when the issuer explicitly says that profit met a plan, forecast or expectation, or was unchanged. ‘Loss’ requires an explicit realised net or operating loss. Releases without such wording remain unclassified and are excluded from the conditional estimates.

Variance is reported in squared percentage points. Abnormal return is the share return minus the equal-weight Baltic-market return over the same horizon.

**Kruskal–Wallis test across the available outcome groups**

At least two outcome groups with two observations each are required; this share does not have enough observations for the omnibus test.

**Pairwise result:** No pairwise difference survives BH adjustment.

The test describes historical association. Small groups, overlapping horizons and repeated releases from the same company limit causal interpretation.

<summary>Mean return and five-year average dividend yield versus all portfolios</summary>

![APG1L mean return and historical dividend yield with all portfolios](figures/return_dividend_all_portfolios.png?v=9b46f9677dcd)

The selected share is highlighted, while every other eligible Baltic share is shown as an unlabelled transparent background point. The horizontal coordinate is the realised mean one-period return. The vertical coordinate is the five-year average annual historical dividend yield: each ex-dividend amount is divided by the latest available share price on or before that ex-dividend date, annual event yields are summed, and the five calendar years 2022–2026 are averaged including zero-payment years. Portfolio values are weight-averaged constituent yields. This is descriptive and is not a dividend forecast.

**Execution rationale:** Allocation target is higher, but technical timing does not support buying now.

![GRG1L Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/GRG1L_technicals_6m.png?v=84e5e7c7358b)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 1.0100 | ≤ EUR 0.9944 | ≥ EUR 1.0210 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 51.67 | ≤ EUR 0.9748 | ≥ EUR 1.0454 | HOLD |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 1.000 | ≤ EUR 0.9959 | ≥ EUR 1.0057 | SELL |
| MACD crossover | MACD = -0.0019<br>Signal = -0.0024<br>Gap = +0.0005<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 1.0023 | — | — | BUY |
| Consensus | BUY 1/4; SELL 1/4; neutral 2/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 1.8750 | ≤ EUR 1.7805 | ≥ EUR 1.8885 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 77.76 | ≤ EUR 1.7237 | ≥ EUR 1.8645 | SELL |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.559 | ≤ EUR 1.8705 | ≥ EUR 1.8778 | HOLD |
| MACD crossover | MACD = 0.0244<br>Signal = 0.0217<br>Gap = +0.0028<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 1.8314 | — | — | BUY |
| Consensus | BUY 1/4; SELL 1/4; neutral 2/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

![PZV1L Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/PZV1L_technicals_6m.png?v=3e6ac4fa8128)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 1.7900 | ≤ EUR 1.7621 | ≥ EUR 1.8089 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 56.97 | ≤ EUR 1.6988 | ≥ EUR 1.8340 | HOLD |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.618 | ≤ EUR 1.7788 | ≥ EUR 1.7962 | HOLD |
| MACD crossover | MACD = 0.0059<br>Signal = 0.0067<br>Gap = -0.0008<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 1.8022 | — | — | SELL |
| Consensus | BUY 0/4; SELL 1/4; neutral 3/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

<details markdown="1" class="earnings-outcomes">
<summary>Profit outcome and subsequent price analysis (3 classified of 17 earnings releases)</summary>

Higher/lower profit refers to the issuer's explicit comparison with the earlier comparable period. ‘In line / unchanged’ is used only when the issuer explicitly says that profit met a plan, forecast or expectation, or was unchanged. ‘Loss’ requires an explicit realised net or operating loss. Releases without such wording remain unclassified and are excluded from the conditional estimates.

Variance is reported in squared percentage points. Abnormal return is the share return minus the equal-weight Baltic-market return over the same horizon.

**Kruskal–Wallis test across the available outcome groups**

At least two outcome groups with two observations each are required; this share does not have enough observations for the omnibus test.

**Pairwise result:** No pairwise difference survives BH adjustment.

The test describes historical association. Small groups, overlapping horizons and repeated releases from the same company limit causal interpretation.

The selected share is highlighted, while every other eligible Baltic share is shown as an unlabelled transparent background point. The horizontal coordinate is the realised mean one-period return. The vertical coordinate is the five-year average annual historical dividend yield: each ex-dividend amount is divided by the latest available share price on or before that ex-dividend date, annual event yields are summed, and the five calendar years 2022–2026 are averaged including zero-payment years. Portfolio values are weight-averaged constituent yields. This is descriptive and is not a dividend forecast.

![TAL1T Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/TAL1T_technicals_6m.png?v=d537259c661d)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 0.6470 | ≤ EUR 0.6432 | ≥ EUR 0.6499 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 57.44 | ≤ EUR 0.6267 | ≥ EUR 0.6563 | HOLD |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.290 | ≤ EUR 0.6465 | ≥ EUR 0.6510 | HOLD |
| MACD crossover | MACD = 0.0023<br>Signal = 0.0029<br>Gap = -0.0006<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 0.6568 | — | — | SELL |
| Consensus | BUY 0/4; SELL 1/4; neutral 3/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

<summary>Profit outcome and subsequent price analysis (17 classified of 27 earnings releases)</summary>

Higher/lower profit refers to the issuer's explicit comparison with the earlier comparable period. ‘In line / unchanged’ is used only when the issuer explicitly says that profit met a plan, forecast or expectation, or was unchanged. ‘Loss’ requires an explicit realised net or operating loss. Releases without such wording remain unclassified and are excluded from the conditional estimates.

Variance is reported in squared percentage points. Abnormal return is the share return minus the equal-weight Baltic-market return over the same horizon.

| Horizon | Groups | N | H | Raw p | BH-adjusted p | Conclusion |

| 1d | 3 | 17 | 2.179 | 0.3364 | 0.7067 | No adjusted evidence |

**Pairwise result:** No pairwise difference survives BH adjustment.

The test describes historical association. Small groups, overlapping horizons and repeated releases from the same company limit causal interpretation.

<summary>Mean return and five-year average dividend yield versus all portfolios</summary>

![TAL1T mean return and historical dividend yield with all portfolios](figures/return_dividend_all_portfolios.png?v=9b46f9677dcd)

The selected share is highlighted, while every other eligible Baltic share is shown as an unlabelled transparent background point. The horizontal coordinate is the realised mean one-period return. The vertical coordinate is the five-year average annual historical dividend yield: each ex-dividend amount is divided by the latest available share price on or before that ex-dividend date, annual event yields are summed, and the five calendar years 2022–2026 are averaged including zero-payment years. Portfolio values are weight-averaged constituent yields. This is descriptive and is not a dividend forecast.

![TEL1L Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/TEL1L_technicals_6m.png?v=1537f4316ee6)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 2.2500 | ≤ EUR 2.2122 | ≥ EUR 2.3018 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 51.23 | ≤ EUR 2.1600 | ≥ EUR 2.3162 | HOLD |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.167 | ≤ EUR 2.2534 | ≥ EUR 2.3832 | BUY |
| MACD crossover | MACD = 0.0083<br>Signal = 0.0122<br>Gap = -0.0039<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 2.3115 | — | — | SELL |
| Consensus | BUY 1/4; SELL 1/4; neutral 2/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

<summary>Mean return and five-year average dividend yield versus all portfolios</summary>

![TEL1L mean return and historical dividend yield with all portfolios](figures/return_dividend_all_portfolios.png?v=9b46f9677dcd)

The selected share is highlighted, while every other eligible Baltic share is shown as an unlabelled transparent background point. The horizontal coordinate is the realised mean one-period return. The vertical coordinate is the five-year average annual historical dividend yield: each ex-dividend amount is divided by the latest available share price on or before that ex-dividend date, annual event yields are summed, and the five calendar years 2022–2026 are averaged including zero-payment years. Portfolio values are weight-averaged constituent yields. This is descriptive and is not a dividend forecast.

![DGR1R Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/DGR1R_technicals_6m.png?v=64d1b0522acb)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 1.7150 | ≤ EUR 1.6663 | ≥ EUR 1.7512 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 60.81 | ≤ EUR 1.5413 | ≥ EUR 1.7601 | HOLD |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.073 | ≤ EUR 1.7184 | ≥ EUR 1.7466 | BUY |
| MACD crossover | MACD = 0.0274<br>Signal = 0.0321<br>Gap = -0.0047<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 1.7893 | — | — | SELL |
| Consensus | BUY 1/4; SELL 1/4; neutral 2/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

<summary>Profit outcome and subsequent price analysis (13 classified of 16 earnings releases)</summary>

Higher/lower profit refers to the issuer's explicit comparison with the earlier comparable period. ‘In line / unchanged’ is used only when the issuer explicitly says that profit met a plan, forecast or expectation, or was unchanged. ‘Loss’ requires an explicit realised net or operating loss. Releases without such wording remain unclassified and are excluded from the conditional estimates.

Variance is reported in squared percentage points. Abnormal return is the share return minus the equal-weight Baltic-market return over the same horizon.

At least two outcome groups with two observations each are required; this share does not have enough observations for the omnibus test.

**Pairwise result:** No pairwise difference survives BH adjustment.

The test describes historical association. Small groups, overlapping horizons and repeated releases from the same company limit causal interpretation.

![DGR1R mean return and historical dividend yield with all portfolios](figures/return_dividend_all_portfolios.png?v=9b46f9677dcd)

The selected share is highlighted, while every other eligible Baltic share is shown as an unlabelled transparent background point. The horizontal coordinate is the realised mean one-period return. The vertical coordinate is the five-year average annual historical dividend yield: each ex-dividend amount is divided by the latest available share price on or before that ex-dividend date, annual event yields are summed, and the five calendar years 2022–2026 are averaged including zero-payment years. Portfolio values are weight-averaged constituent yields. This is descriptive and is not a dividend forecast.

![HAE1T Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/HAE1T_technicals_6m.png?v=f8e0e7c1733f)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 5.2000 | ≤ EUR 5.0878 | ≥ EUR 5.4702 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 46.22 | ≤ EUR 4.7403 | ≥ EUR 5.8473 | HOLD |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.000 | ≤ EUR 5.3176 | ≥ EUR 5.8231 | BUY |
| MACD crossover | MACD = 0.0070<br>Signal = 0.0245<br>Gap = -0.0175<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 5.4747 | — | — | SELL |
| Consensus | BUY 1/4; SELL 1/4; neutral 2/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

<details markdown="1" class="earnings-outcomes">
<summary>Profit outcome and subsequent price analysis (16 classified of 19 earnings releases)</summary>

Higher/lower profit refers to the issuer's explicit comparison with the earlier comparable period. ‘In line / unchanged’ is used only when the issuer explicitly says that profit met a plan, forecast or expectation, or was unchanged. ‘Loss’ requires an explicit realised net or operating loss. Releases without such wording remain unclassified and are excluded from the conditional estimates.

Variance is reported in squared percentage points. Abnormal return is the share return minus the equal-weight Baltic-market return over the same horizon.

**Pairwise result:** No pairwise difference survives BH adjustment.

The test describes historical association. Small groups, overlapping horizons and repeated releases from the same company limit causal interpretation.

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Mean return and five-year average dividend yield versus all portfolios</summary>

![HAE1T mean return and historical dividend yield with all portfolios](figures/return_dividend_all_portfolios.png?v=9b46f9677dcd)

The selected share is highlighted, while every other eligible Baltic share is shown as an unlabelled transparent background point. The horizontal coordinate is the realised mean one-period return. The vertical coordinate is the five-year average annual historical dividend yield: each ex-dividend amount is divided by the latest available share price on or before that ex-dividend date, annual event yields are summed, and the five calendar years 2022–2026 are averaged including zero-payment years. Portfolio values are weight-averaged constituent yields. This is descriptive and is not a dividend forecast.

![LHV1T Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/LHV1T_technicals_6m.png?v=9d03842586cd)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 3.2500 | ≤ EUR 3.2443 | ≥ EUR 3.2917 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 39.71 | ≤ EUR 3.2051 | ≥ EUR 3.3700 | HOLD |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.255 | ≤ EUR 3.2457 | ≥ EUR 3.2830 | HOLD |
| MACD crossover | MACD = -0.0084<br>Signal = -0.0087<br>Gap = +0.0002<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 3.2464 | — | — | BUY |
| Consensus | BUY 1/4; SELL 0/4; neutral 3/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

<summary>Profit outcome and subsequent price analysis (16 classified of 18 earnings releases)</summary>

Higher/lower profit refers to the issuer's explicit comparison with the earlier comparable period. ‘In line / unchanged’ is used only when the issuer explicitly says that profit met a plan, forecast or expectation, or was unchanged. ‘Loss’ requires an explicit realised net or operating loss. Releases without such wording remain unclassified and are excluded from the conditional estimates.

Variance is reported in squared percentage points. Abnormal return is the share return minus the equal-weight Baltic-market return over the same horizon.

| Horizon | Groups | N | H | Raw p | BH-adjusted p | Conclusion |

| 1d | 2 | 15 | 0.462 | 0.4969 | 0.7846 | No adjusted evidence |

**Pairwise result:** No pairwise difference survives BH adjustment.

The test describes historical association. Small groups, overlapping horizons and repeated releases from the same company limit causal interpretation.

![LHV1T mean return and historical dividend yield with all portfolios](figures/return_dividend_all_portfolios.png?v=9b46f9677dcd)

The selected share is highlighted, while every other eligible Baltic share is shown as an unlabelled transparent background point. The horizontal coordinate is the realised mean one-period return. The vertical coordinate is the five-year average annual historical dividend yield: each ex-dividend amount is divided by the latest available share price on or before that ex-dividend date, annual event yields are summed, and the five calendar years 2022–2026 are averaged including zero-payment years. Portfolio values are weight-averaged constituent yields. This is descriptive and is not a dividend forecast.

![CPA1T Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/CPA1T_technicals_6m.png?v=7a5e4719592f)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 2.3750 | ≤ EUR 2.3222 | ≥ EUR 2.3933 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 56.11 | ≤ EUR 2.2234 | ≥ EUR 2.4556 | HOLD |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.331 | ≤ EUR 2.3674 | ≥ EUR 2.4166 | HOLD |
| MACD crossover | MACD = 0.0102<br>Signal = 0.0088<br>Gap = +0.0014<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 2.3526 | — | — | BUY |
| Consensus | BUY 1/4; SELL 0/4; neutral 3/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

<summary>Profit outcome and subsequent price analysis (22 classified of 23 earnings releases)</summary>

Higher/lower profit refers to the issuer's explicit comparison with the earlier comparable period. ‘In line / unchanged’ is used only when the issuer explicitly says that profit met a plan, forecast or expectation, or was unchanged. ‘Loss’ requires an explicit realised net or operating loss. Releases without such wording remain unclassified and are excluded from the conditional estimates.

Variance is reported in squared percentage points. Abnormal return is the share return minus the equal-weight Baltic-market return over the same horizon.

The selected share is highlighted, while every other eligible Baltic share is shown as an unlabelled transparent background point. The horizontal coordinate is the realised mean one-period return. **Execution rationale:** The optimiser does not require a position change.

![SAF1R Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/SAF1R_technicals_6m.png?v=14624b71def5)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 16.5000 | ≤ EUR 16.1200 | ≥ EUR 16.8000 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 51.39 | ≤ EUR 15.2897 | ≥ EUR 17.5532 | HOLD |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 1.000 | ≤ EUR 16.1626 | ≥ EUR 16.4266 | SELL |
| MACD crossover | MACD = -0.0493<br>Signal = -0.0428<br>Gap = -0.0065<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 16.6015 | — | — | SELL |
| Consensus | BUY 0/4; SELL 2/4; neutral 2/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

Higher/lower profit refers to the issuer's explicit comparison with the earlier comparable period. ‘In line / unchanged’ is used only when the issuer explicitly says that profit met a plan, forecast or expectation, or was unchanged. ‘Loss’ requires an explicit realised net or operating loss. Variance is reported in squared percentage points. Abnormal return is the share return minus the equal-weight Baltic-market return over the same horizon.

**Kruskal–Wallis test across the available outcome groups**

| Horizon | Groups | N | H | Raw p | BH-adjusted p | Conclusion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1d | 2 | 9 | 5.400 | 0.0201 | 0.3021 | No adjusted evidence |
| 5d | 2 | 9 | 4.267 | 0.0389 | 0.3579 | No adjusted evidence |
| 21d | 2 | 9 | 2.400 | 0.1213 | 0.5365 | No adjusted evidence |

**Pairwise result:** No pairwise difference survives BH adjustment.

The test describes historical association. Small groups, overlapping horizons and repeated releases from the same company limit causal interpretation.

![SAF1R mean return and historical dividend yield with all portfolios](figures/return_dividend_all_portfolios.png?v=9b46f9677dcd)

The selected share is highlighted, while every other eligible Baltic share is shown as an unlabelled transparent background point. The horizontal coordinate is the realised mean one-period return. The vertical coordinate is the five-year average annual historical dividend yield: each ex-dividend amount is divided by the latest available share price on or before that ex-dividend date, annual event yields are summed, and the five calendar years 2022–2026 are averaged including zero-payment years. Portfolio values are weight-averaged constituent yields. This is descriptive and is not a dividend forecast.

**Execution rationale:** The optimiser does not require a position change.

![TSM1T Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/TSM1T_technicals_6m.png?v=4fc7bd006b1d)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 1.1920 | ≤ EUR 1.1914 | ≥ EUR 1.2168 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 35.11 | ≤ EUR 1.1834 | ≥ EUR 1.2483 | HOLD |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.144 | ≤ EUR 1.1933 | ≥ EUR 1.2028 | BUY |
| MACD crossover | MACD = -0.0058<br>Signal = -0.0049<br>Gap = -0.0009<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 1.2059 | — | — | SELL |
| Consensus | BUY 1/4; SELL 1/4; neutral 2/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

<details markdown="1" class="earnings-outcomes">
<summary>Profit outcome and subsequent price analysis (14 classified of 15 earnings releases)</summary>

Higher/lower profit refers to the issuer's explicit comparison with the earlier comparable period. ‘In line / unchanged’ is used only when the issuer explicitly says that profit met a plan, forecast or expectation, or was unchanged. ‘Loss’ requires an explicit realised net or operating loss. Releases without such wording remain unclassified and are excluded from the conditional estimates.

Variance is reported in squared percentage points. Abnormal return is the share return minus the equal-weight Baltic-market return over the same horizon.

**Kruskal–Wallis test across the available outcome groups**

| Horizon | Groups | N | H | Raw p | BH-adjusted p | Conclusion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1d | 2 | 14 | 0.300 | 0.5839 | 0.7962 | No adjusted evidence |

| 21d | 2 | 14 | 0.033 | 0.8551 | 0.9484 | No adjusted evidence |

**Pairwise result:** No pairwise difference survives BH adjustment.

The test describes historical association. Small groups, overlapping horizons and repeated releases from the same company limit causal interpretation.

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Mean return and five-year average dividend yield versus all portfolios</summary>

![TSM1T mean return and historical dividend yield with all portfolios](figures/return_dividend_all_portfolios.png?v=9b46f9677dcd)

The selected share is highlighted, while every other eligible Baltic share is shown as an unlabelled transparent background point. The horizontal coordinate is the realised mean one-period return. The vertical coordinate is the five-year average annual historical dividend yield: each ex-dividend amount is divided by the latest available share price on or before that ex-dividend date, annual event yields are summed, and the five calendar years 2022–2026 are averaged including zero-payment years. Portfolio values are weight-averaged constituent yields. This is descriptive and is not a dividend forecast.

![TKM1T Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/TKM1T_technicals_6m.png?v=dd8b565b5660)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 8.8800 | ≤ EUR 8.8359 | ≥ EUR 9.0431 | HOLD |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 28.70 | ≤ EUR 8.8834 | ≥ EUR 9.1348 | BUY |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.409 | ≤ EUR 8.8636 | ≥ EUR 8.8921 | HOLD |
| MACD crossover | MACD = -0.0401<br>Signal = -0.0393<br>Gap = -0.0008<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 8.8924 | — | — | SELL |
| Consensus | BUY 1/4; SELL 1/4; neutral 2/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | HOLD |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

<details markdown="1" class="earnings-outcomes">
<summary>Profit outcome and subsequent price analysis (15 classified of 19 earnings releases)</summary>

Higher/lower profit refers to the issuer's explicit comparison with the earlier comparable period. ‘In line / unchanged’ is used only when the issuer explicitly says that profit met a plan, forecast or expectation, or was unchanged. ‘Loss’ requires an explicit realised net or operating loss. Releases without such wording remain unclassified and are excluded from the conditional estimates.

Variance is reported in squared percentage points. Abnormal return is the share return minus the equal-weight Baltic-market return over the same horizon.

**Kruskal–Wallis test across the available outcome groups**

| Horizon | Groups | N | H | Raw p | BH-adjusted p | Conclusion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1d | 2 | 14 | 1.604 | 0.2053 | 0.6158 | No adjusted evidence |
| 5d | 2 | 14 | 0.040 | 0.8415 | 0.9484 | No adjusted evidence |
| 21d | 2 | 14 | 2.351 | 0.1252 | 0.5365 | No adjusted evidence |

**Pairwise result:** No pairwise difference survives BH adjustment.

The test describes historical association. Small groups, overlapping horizons and repeated releases from the same company limit causal interpretation.

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Mean return and five-year average dividend yield versus all portfolios</summary>

![TKM1T mean return and historical dividend yield with all portfolios](figures/return_dividend_all_portfolios.png?v=9b46f9677dcd)

The selected share is highlighted, while every other eligible Baltic share is shown as an unlabelled transparent background point. The horizontal coordinate is the realised mean one-period return. The vertical coordinate is the five-year average annual historical dividend yield: each ex-dividend amount is divided by the latest available share price on or before that ex-dividend date, annual event yields are summed, and the five calendar years 2022–2026 are averaged including zero-payment years. Portfolio values are weight-averaged constituent yields. This is descriptive and is not a dividend forecast.

![ROE1L Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI and Stochastic RSI — last 126 observations](figures/stock_profiles/ROE1L_technicals_6m.png?v=42c0158fe7d8)

Signals combine four indicators: Bollinger bands, RSI, MACD and Stochastic RSI. Vertical lines distinguish 4-of-4, 3-of-4 and 2-of-4 buy/sell agreement.

**Current indicative prices and four-indicator signals**

| Indicator | Current indicator value | BUY price | SELL price | Signal now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bollinger price | Close = EUR 0.8190 | ≤ EUR 0.8433 | ≥ EUR 0.9122 | BUY |
| RSI(14) | RSI = 18.07 | ≤ EUR 0.8476 | ≥ EUR 0.9598 | BUY |
| Stochastic RSI %K | %K = 0.000 | ≤ EUR 0.8453 | ≥ EUR 0.8671 | BUY |
| MACD crossover | MACD = -0.0096<br>Signal = -0.0040<br>Gap = -0.0055<br>Bullish crossover close ≈ EUR 0.9059 | — | — | SELL |
| Consensus | BUY 3/4; SELL 1/4; neutral 0/4 | At least 3 BUY votes | At least 3 SELL votes | BUY |

MACD does not define an acceptable purchase or sale price. Its bullish crossover close is only the hypothetical latest close at which MACD would cross above its signal line if all earlier closes stayed unchanged. A crossover above the current price means that upward momentum still needs confirmation; it does not mean that the investor should wait and buy at that higher price. RSI and Stochastic RSI price thresholds are also indicative because only the latest close is varied. The four-indicator consensus is BUY or SELL only when at least three indicators agree; otherwise it is HOLD.

<details markdown="1" class="earnings-outcomes">
<summary>Profit outcome and subsequent price analysis (2 classified of 8 earnings releases)</summary>

Higher/lower profit refers to the issuer's explicit comparison with the earlier comparable period. ‘In line / unchanged’ is used only when the issuer explicitly says that profit met a plan, forecast or expectation, or was unchanged. ‘Loss’ requires an explicit realised net or operating loss. Releases without such wording remain unclassified and are excluded from the conditional estimates.

Variance is reported in squared percentage points. Abnormal return is the share return minus the equal-weight Baltic-market return over the same horizon.

| Higher profit | 5d | 2 | 0.45% | 0.028 | 0.45% | 100% | 0.22% | 0.089 | 0.22% |
| Higher profit | 21d | 2 | 0.08% | 6.042 | 0.08% | 50% | 0.65% | 0.482 | 0.65% |

**Kruskal–Wallis test across the available outcome groups**

At least two outcome groups with two observations each are required; this share does not have enough observations for the omnibus test.

**Pairwise result:** No pairwise difference survives BH adjustment.

The test describes historical association. Small groups, overlapping horizons and repeated releases from the same company limit causal interpretation.

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Mean return and five-year average dividend yield versus all portfolios</summary>

![ROE1L mean return and historical dividend yield with all portfolios](figures/return_dividend_all_portfolios.png?v=9b46f9677dcd)

The selected share is highlighted, while every other eligible Baltic share is shown as an unlabelled transparent background point. The horizontal coordinate is the realised mean one-period return. The vertical coordinate is the five-year average annual historical dividend yield: each ex-dividend amount is divided by the latest available share price on or before that ex-dividend date, annual event yields are summed, and the five calendar years 2022–2026 are averaged including zero-payment years. Portfolio values are weight-averaged constituent yields. This is descriptive and is not a dividend forecast.

<details markdown="1">
<summary><strong>Figure 2.e. SSD pairwise dominance matrix used by netSD</strong></summary>

A blue cell equals 1 when the row entity SSD-dominates the column entity. Row sums contribute to OUT; column sums contribute to IN.

<a href="figures/netsd_reference_SSD_matrix.png?v=ea11b2369222" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><img src="figures/netsd_reference_SSD_matrix.png?v=ea11b2369222" alt="SSD pairwise dominance matrix used by netSD"></a>

</details>

<details markdown="1">
<summary><strong>Figure 2.f. TSD pairwise dominance matrix used by netSD</strong></summary>

A blue cell equals 1 when the row entity TSD-dominates the column entity, including the required mean-return condition.

<a href="figures/netsd_reference_TSD_matrix.png?v=8589006281dc" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><img src="figures/netsd_reference_TSD_matrix.png?v=8589006281dc" alt="TSD pairwise dominance matrix used by netSD"></a>

</details>

<details markdown="1">
<summary><strong>Figure 2.g. Combined FSD + SSD + TSD matrix used to calculate netSD</strong></summary>

Each cell is the sum of the three order-specific indicators and therefore ranges from 0 to 3. For every entity, OUT is its combined row sum and IN is its combined column sum. The fixed denominator is 119, so netSD = (OUT − IN) / 119. This is the exact fixed comparison matrix underlying the reported optimisation scores.

<a href="figures/netsd_reference_all_orders_matrix.png?v=1bfe99a3807b" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><img src="figures/netsd_reference_all_orders_matrix.png?v=1bfe99a3807b" alt="Combined dominance matrix used to calculate netSD"></a>

</details>

The five-year average yield uses ex-dividend amounts divided by the latest available price on or before each ex-date. Current- and update-quantity dividend amounts use the five-year average annual dividend per share; they are historical gross scenarios, not forecasts.

allocation_change_direction describes the optimiser's target relative to current holdings. It is not the current execution recommendation; use current_execution_decision in the canonical trade table and interactive share profiles for that purpose.

<details markdown="1" class="systemic-risk-section">
<summary><strong>VAR, VECM, GARCH and DCC connectedness</strong></summary>

The connectedness analysis follows the VAR/VECM and generalized forecast-error variance-decomposition logic used by [Kabašinskas (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13362-024-00144-x). The main network contains every investment-admissible share, all 12 funds and the S&P 500; the portfolio network is retained as a secondary comparison. The arrowhead identifies the direction: A → B means that shocks in A explain part of B's forecast-error variance. An asterisk (*) after a value means that this direction is significant in the corresponding Granger-causality test at 5%. **Red nodes are net receivers (TO − FROM < 0); blue nodes are net transmitters (TO − FROM > 0).** Node area increases with |TO − FROM|, so a larger node has a stronger net role.

**Model-assumption checks are shown before the results.** ADF tests should reject a unit root for VAR returns. VECM requires non-stationary levels, stationary first differences and a cointegration rank strictly between zero and the number of variables. Stability is required for VAR. The residual-whiteness p-value should exceed 0.05. Multivariate normality fails in every case, which is common for financial returns but makes Gaussian small-sample inference less reliable. The high-dimensional Johansen critical values are outside the tabulated range of the software, so the share VECM rank is exploratory. A failed row is displayed for comparison and must not be treated as a validated structural model.

<details markdown="1" open>
<summary><strong>Model assumptions and diagnostic tests</strong></summary>

| Universe | Model | stationary levels | stationary returns | rank | stable | whiteness p | normality p | assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shares | VAR(1) | 4/34 | 34/34 | – | Yes | 0.0001 | 0.0000 | Fail / diagnostic only |
| Shares | VECM(rank=22, diff_lags=0) | 4/34 | 34/34 | 22 | – | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | Fail / diagnostic only |
| Portfolios | VAR(1) | 0/8 | 8/8 | – | Yes | 0.1711 | 0.0000 | Pass |
| Portfolios | VECM(rank=1, diff_lags=0) | 0/8 | 8/8 | 1 | – | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | Fail / diagnostic only |

</details>

<div class="systemic-model-grid">
<section><h4>VAR</h4><p>VAR uses daily returns and a BIC-selected lag. Stability, residual whiteness and normality are rechecked after adding funds; the diagnostic table above determines whether each fit is acceptable.</p><p><strong>Shares, all funds and S&amp;P 500</strong></p><img src="figures/spillover_shares_var_network.png?v=422dff64a17d" alt="VAR spillover network including funds"><p><strong>All update portfolios and S&amp;P 500</strong></p><img src="figures/spillover_portfolios_var_network.png?v=895f59b3926e" alt="VAR spillover network including Update3"></section>
<section><h4>VECM</h4><p>VECM uses cumulative log-return levels. The cointegration rank and residual tests are recalculated for the expanded instrument set; high-dimensional rank estimates remain exploratory.</p><p><strong>Shares, all funds and S&amp;P 500</strong></p><img src="figures/spillover_shares_vecm_network.png?v=18aa188f6eea" alt="VECM spillover network including funds"><p><strong>All update portfolios and S&amp;P 500</strong></p><img src="figures/spillover_portfolios_vecm_network.png?v=43bf5d9fe5c2" alt="VECM spillover network including Update3"></section>
</div>

<details markdown="1" open>
<summary><strong>120-observation rolling overall spillover for every model version</strong></summary>

Following the rolling-window implementation used in the cited study, each point re-estimates the model from the latest 120 common observations and reports the generalized-FEVD Total Spillover Index. The plot contains the share VAR and VECM, portfolio VAR and VECM, and the VAR fitted to liquidity-corrected GARCH log variances. This shows how overall connectedness changes through time rather than reducing every model to one full-sample number.

![120-observation rolling total spillover](figures/spillover_total_rolling_120_all_versions.png?v=28489049e1c1)

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="garch-systemic-risk" open>
<summary><strong>GARCH volatility spillover and DCC-GARCH</strong></summary>

The GARCH analysis uses a retrospective non-trading correction before model estimation. Consecutive zero returns are treated as stale-price days: the next observed non-zero log return is spread equally over that zero-return spell and its trade day. Corrected returns are then winsorised at the 0.5% and 99.5% quantiles. Shares with more than 40% zero-return observations are excluded from this subsection. This correction reduces stale-price distortion but is an explicit modelling assumption and must not be interpreted as observed daily price movement.

The filter excludes **RSU1L, TEL1L, TVE1T** from the GARCH/DCC system only. They remain in the other portfolio analyses. After filtering, 31 series and 857 common observations remain.

#### Liquidity-corrected GARCH variance spillover

Each retained series is fitted with a Student-t GARCH(1,1). A VAR is then fitted to the log conditional variances, and its 10-step generalized FEVD produces directional volatility spillovers. The enlarged arrowhead shows the direction of predictive transmission between conditional variances. An asterisk marks variance Granger causality at 5%; red nodes are net volatility receivers, blue nodes are net transmitters, and node area increases with |TO − FROM|.

![Liquidity-corrected GARCH variance spillover](figures/garch_corrected_variance_spillover.png?v=fd0eb158112c)

The corrected-volatility Total Spillover Index is **41.57%**. **18 of 31** univariate fits still have α + β ≥ 0.99, so volatility persistence remains close to the IGARCH boundary and the long-horizon interpretation requires caution.

<details markdown="1">
<summary><strong>DCC-GARCH conditional correlations (not spillover)</strong></summary>

Following [Engle (2002)](https://doi.org/10.1198/073500102288618487), standardized residuals from the univariate GARCH models enter the two-step Dynamic Conditional Correlation recursion. DCC is an undirected conditional-dependence model and must not be read as Granger causality or directional shock transmission. The left panel is a hierarchically clustered heatmap of average conditional correlations. The upper-right panel shows their mean absolute strength through time; the lower-right panel shows the five pairs with the strongest average DCC. The parameters are estimated from six starting values to guard against a local boundary solution.

![DCC-GARCH conditional-correlation heatmap and dynamics](figures/dcc_garch_network_and_dynamic_correlation.png?v=7b40ee1c29b4)

The estimated DCC parameters are α = **0.0107**, β = **0.7664**, and α + β = **0.7771**; optimiser convergence = **True**. The very small DCC persistence means that, after the stale-price correction, the estimated conditional-correlation system is close to a constant-correlation model with brief isolated spikes rather than a slowly evolving dependence process.

</details>

Median daily turnover and zero-volume frequency use official Nasdaq Baltic price-volume observations from the last 365 calendar days of the sample. Trade-to-turnover is the proposed absolute order value divided by median daily turnover. HIGH flags median turnover below EUR 5,000 or an order above 20% of median turnover; MEDIUM flags below EUR 20,000 or above 10%. These are transparent screening thresholds, not a guarantee of execution. HIGH trades should be split, limited or omitted after checking the live order book.

The number of holdings is not a diversification measure. Top-five and top-ten shares show how much capital is concentrated in the largest positions; HHI and the effective number of positions measure weight concentration. Country, list, industry and supersector totals expose common economic exposures that a position count conceals. Very small positions add trading complexity while making little difference to risk.

### In-sample, out-of-sample and complete-period validation









netSD counts outgoing minus incoming FSD, SSD and TSD relations relative to a fixed comparison network. It has no monetary unit and does not state expected profit, maximum loss or suitability for an investor. Use it as a distribution-ranking signal together with return, volatility, drawdown, VaR/ES, liquidity, concentration and cost results.

The S&P 500 series is a USD price-index benchmark. It excludes dividends and has not been converted into EUR investor returns, so it is retained only as a broad market sensitivity reference. Direct performance claims require a total-return benchmark converted to EUR over identical dates.

Dividend values are historical gross cash distributions. They are excluded from optimisation and are neither a forecast nor an assessment of dividend sustainability. Company valuation, earnings quality, debt, free cash flow and payout coverage have not been modelled; each proposed purchase therefore requires a separate fundamental review.

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="report-section" id="analytics-2-14">
<summary><strong>2.14. Model</strong></summary>
<h3>Update3: shares and funds in the penalised netSD model</h3>

Let $q_i$ be integer stock quantities, $u_f$ integer fund units, $p_i$ share prices and $v_f$ published EUR NAV. Portfolio weights are their invested EUR values divided by total invested capital. Fund NAV returns already include recurring expenses.

$$\max_{\mathbf q,\mathbf u}\quad \operatorname{netSD}(\mathbf w)-\lambda_N N_{\mathrm{new,shares}}^2-\lambda_E\frac{1}{\sum_jw_j^2}-\lambda_S P_{\mathrm{small,new,shares}}-\lambda_D P_{\mathrm{dividend,shares}}$$

$$\sum_i p_iq_i+\sum_fv_fu_f\le15000,\qquad q_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0},\quad u_f\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0},\quad\sum_jw_j=1.$$

$$2\le\sum_fz_f\le4,\quad z_f\in\{0,1\},\quad0.02z_f\le w_f\le z_f.$$

$$q_i\ge q_i^{\mathrm{Current}}\quad\text{in the no-sales case};\qquad \boldsymbol\mu^\top\mathbf w\ge\mu_{\mathrm{Current}}.$$

New stock purchases are either zero or at least 10 shares. Funds use whole units and are exempt from the cash-dividend shortfall penalty because the selected C classes accumulate income. Estimated embedded annual expense is $\sum_f(v_fu_f)c_f$; it is disclosed in EUR and is not subtracted from net NAV returns a second time. No fund is compulsory. The Russia exclusion, when Emerging Europe is selected, follows its mandate; the absence of China is monitored from published holdings and is not a permanent contractual exclusion.


### Exact mathematical formulation of the netSD portfolio

For share $j$ and observation $t$, let $R_{tj}$ be the return, $w_j$ the portfolio weight and

$$r_{p,t}=\sum_{j=1}^{n}w_jR_{tj},\qquad \sum_{j=1}^{n}w_j=1,\qquad w_j\ge0.$$

For entity $i$, define the empirical distribution and its successive integrals by

$$H_i^{(1)}(x)=F_i(x),\qquad H_i^{(q)}(x)=\int_{-\infty}^{x}H_i^{(q-1)}(u)\,du,\quad q=2,3.$$

Entity $i$ dominates entity $k$ at order $q$ when

$$H_i^{(q)}(x)\le H_k^{(q)}(x)\quad\text{for every observed support point }x,$$

with strict inequality for at least one point. Third-order dominance additionally requires $\mathbb E(R_i)\ge\mathbb E(R_k)$. Write $a_{ik}^{(q)}=1$ when these conditions hold and zero otherwise. Then

$$\operatorname{OUT}(p)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\sum_{q=1}^{3}a_{pk}^{(q)},\qquad \operatorname{IN}(p)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\sum_{q=1}^{3}a_{kp}^{(q)},$$

$$\boxed{\operatorname{netSD}(p)=\frac{\operatorname{OUT}(p)-\operatorname{IN}(p)}{D}},\qquad D=\max_i\{\operatorname{OUT}(i)+\operatorname{IN}(i)\}.$$

The unpenalised portfolio problem is

$$\boxed{\max_{\mathbf w}\;\operatorname{netSD}(\mathbf w)}$$

subject to

$$\sum_jw_j=1,\qquad w_j\ge0,\qquad \boldsymbol\mu^\top\mathbf w\ge\mu_{\mathrm{Current}},$$

$$w_j=0\quad\text{if individual }\operatorname{netSD}_j\le0\text{ or the share is outside the admissible universe}.$$

The common-network scores in Section 2.1 supersede numerical score quotes from the previous share-only reference universe. NetSD is discrete and the numerical search does not certify a global optimum.

</details>

const metricModal=document.createElement('div');
metricModal.className='metric-modal';metricModal.hidden=true;
metricModal.innerHTML='<div class="metric-modal-card" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="metric-modal-title"><button type="button" class="metric-modal-close" aria-label="Close">&times;</button><h3 id="metric-modal-title"></h3><p><strong>Meaning:</strong> <span class="metric-modal-meaning"></span></p><p><strong>Calculation:</strong> <span class="metric-modal-calculation"></span></p><p><strong>Interpretation:</strong> <span class="metric-modal-interpretation"></span></p></div>';
document.body.appendChild(metricModal);
function closeMetricModal(){metricModal.hidden=true;}
document.addEventListener('click',function(event){
  const button=event.target.closest('.metric-help-button');
  if(button){metricModal.querySelector('h3').textContent=button.dataset.metric;metricModal.querySelector('.metric-modal-meaning').textContent=button.dataset.meaning;metricModal.querySelector('.metric-modal-calculation').textContent=button.dataset.calculation;metricModal.querySelector('.metric-modal-interpretation').textContent=button.dataset.interpretation;metricModal.hidden=false;metricModal.querySelector('.metric-modal-close').focus();return;}
  if(event.target===metricModal||event.target.closest('.metric-modal-close'))closeMetricModal();
});
document.addEventListener('keydown',function(event){if(event.key==='Escape')closeMetricModal();});
document.querySelectorAll('table.scenario-period-table').forEach(function(table){
  const directions={3:1,4:1,5:-1,6:1,7:1,8:-1,9:-1,10:1,11:-1,12:1};
  const rows=[...table.tBodies[0].rows];
  Object.entries(directions).forEach(([columnText,direction])=>{
    const column=Number(columnText), cells=rows.map(row=>row.cells[column]);
    const values=cells.map(cell=>Number.parseFloat(cell.textContent.replace(/[^0-9eE+.-]/g,'')));
    const finite=values.filter(Number.isFinite); if(!finite.length)return;
    const minimum=Math.min(...finite),maximum=Math.max(...finite),spread=maximum-minimum;
    cells.forEach((cell,index)=>{if(!Number.isFinite(values[index]))return;let score=spread?((values[index]-minimum)/spread):.5;if(direction<0)score=1-score;const hue=120*score;cell.style.backgroundColor=`hsl(${hue} 68% 82%)`;cell.style.color='#17212b';cell.title=`Investor-benefit score within this column: ${(100*score).toFixed(0)}%`;} );
  });
});
document.querySelectorAll('details.stock-profile').forEach(function(profile) {
  profile.addEventListener('toggle', function() {
    if (!profile.open) return;
    document.querySelectorAll('details.stock-profile[open]').forEach(function(other) {
      if (other !== profile) other.open = false;
    });
  });
});
document.querySelectorAll('.profile-filters').forEach(function(filterBlock) {
  const section=filterBlock.closest('details.report-section');
  if (!section) return;
    const signalFilters=[...filterBlock.querySelectorAll('.signal-filters input[type="checkbox"]')];
    const netsdFilters=[...filterBlock.querySelectorAll('.netsd-filters input[type="checkbox"]')];
    const dividendFilters=[...filterBlock.querySelectorAll('.dividend-filters input[type="checkbox"]')];
    const instrumentFilters=[...filterBlock.querySelectorAll('.instrument-type-filters input[type="radio"]')];
    const filters=[...signalFilters,...netsdFilters,...dividendFilters,...instrumentFilters];
  const profiles=[...section.querySelectorAll('details.stock-profile')];
  const counter=filterBlock.querySelector('.profile-filter-count');
  function applyProfileFilters() {
      const selectedSignals=new Set(signalFilters.filter(box=>box.checked).map(box=>box.value));
      const selectedNetsdEffects=new Set(netsdFilters.filter(box=>box.checked).map(box=>box.value));
      const selectedDividendStatuses=new Set(dividendFilters.filter(box=>box.checked).map(box=>box.value));
    const selectedType=instrumentFilters.find(box=>box.checked)?.value || 'ALL';
    let visible=0;
    profiles.forEach(function(profile) {
        const type=profile.classList.contains('fund-profile')?'FUND':'SHARE';
        const show=(selectedType==='ALL'||selectedType===type) && selectedSignals.has(profile.dataset.signal) && selectedNetsdEffects.has(profile.dataset.netsdEffect) && selectedDividendStatuses.has(profile.dataset.dividendStatus);
      profile.hidden=!show;
      if (!show) profile.open=false;
      if (show) visible++;
    });
    if (counter) counter.textContent=`${visible} / ${profiles.length} shown`;
  }
  filters.forEach(box=>box.addEventListener('change',applyProfileFilters));
  applyProfileFilters();
});
document.querySelectorAll('details.portfolio-sensitivity').forEach(function(sensitivity) {
  sensitivity.addEventListener('toggle', function() {
    if (!sensitivity.open) return;
    const components = sensitivity.querySelector('details.dominance-components');
    if (components) components.open = true;
  });
});

function initialiseDominanceExplorer(box) {

    }

      ${profile==='Portfolio'?`<label>Comparison base<select class="dom-benchmark">${benchmarks.map(x=>`<option value="${x}"${x===target?' selected':''}>${displayName(x)}</option>`).join('')}</select></label>`:
      `<label class="dominance-compact-wrap">Comparison portfolios
        <select class="dom-comparators dominance-multiselect dominance-compact-select" multiple size="5">${benchmarks.map(x=>`<option value="${x}"${defaultComparators.has(x)?' selected':''}>${displayName(x)}</option>`).join('')}</select>
        <small>Ctrl/Cmd selects several.</small></label>
       <label class="dominance-compact-wrap">Other shares
        <select class="dom-share-comparators dominance-multiselect dominance-compact-select" multiple size="5">${otherShares.map(x=>`<option value="${x}">${x}</option>`).join('')}</select>
        <small>Optional share comparisons.</small></label>`}
      ${profile==='Portfolio'?`<label class="dominance-multiselect-wrap">Displayed portfolios and shares
        <select class="dominance-multiselect" multiple size="10">

          <optgroup label="Shares">${shareNames.filter(x=>!fundNames.includes(x)).map(x=>`<option value="${x}">${x}</option>`).join('')}</optgroup>
          <optgroup label="Funds">${fundNames.map(x=>`<option value="${x}">${x}</option>`).join('')}</optgroup>

      <label>Horizontal magnification: <output class="dom-hout">8x</output><input class="dom-hzoom" type="range" min="1" max="100" value="8" step="1"></label>
      <button class="dom-save" type="button">Save high-resolution PNG</button>

    const canvas=box.querySelector('canvas'), order=box.querySelector('.dom-order'), benchmark=box.querySelector('.dom-benchmark'), comparators=box.querySelector('.dom-comparators'), shareComparators=box.querySelector('.dom-share-comparators'), multi=profile==='Portfolio'?box.querySelector('.dominance-multiselect'):null, xpos=box.querySelector('.dom-xpos'), hz=box.querySelector('.dom-hzoom'), status=box.querySelector('.dominance-status');
    let centre=.5, hit=[];

      const mid=Math.round(centre*(n-1)), count=Math.max(8,Math.round(n/Number(hz.value))), lo=Math.max(0,Math.min(n-count,mid-Math.floor(count/2))), hi=Math.min(n-1,lo+count-1);
      const comparisonNames=profile==='Portfolio'?names.filter(k=>k!==baseName):selectedComparators.filter(k=>d.series[k]);

      const focus=profile==='Portfolio'?comparisonNames[0]:bench, difference=differences[focus];
      function yrange(i0,i1,keys=names) { let mn=Infinity,mx=-Infinity; keys.forEach(k=>{for(let i=i0;i<=i1;i++){const v=d.series[k][i];if(v<mn)mn=v;if(v>mx)mx=v;}}); if(mx===mn){mx+=1;mn-=1} return [mn,mx]; }
      function arrayRange(a,i0,i1){let mn=Infinity,mx=-Infinity;for(let i=i0;i<=i1;i++){if(a[i]<mn)mn=a[i];if(a[i]>mx)mx=a[i];}if(mx===mn){mx+=1;mn-=1}return[mn,mx];}
      function differenceRange(i0,i1){let mn=Infinity,mx=-Infinity;comparisonNames.forEach(k=>{const r=arrayRange(differences[k],i0,i1);mn=Math.min(mn,r[0]);mx=Math.max(mx,r[1]);});if(mx===mn){mx+=1;mn-=1}return[mn,mx];}
      function axes(p,x0,x1,y0,y1,label) { ctx.strokeStyle='#9aabb5';ctx.lineWidth=1;ctx.beginPath();ctx.moveTo(p.l,p.t);ctx.lineTo(p.l,p.b);ctx.lineTo(p.r,p.b);ctx.stroke();ctx.fillStyle='#263d4b';ctx.fillText(label,p.l,p.t-9); for(let j=0;j<=6;j++){const xx=p.l+(p.r-p.l)*j/6,xv=x0+(x1-x0)*j/6;ctx.fillText(xv.toFixed(5),xx-22,p.b+17);} for(let j=0;j<=5;j++){const yy=p.b-(p.b-p.t)*j/5,yv=y0+(y1-y0)*j/5;ctx.fillText(yv.toExponential(2),Math.max(1,p.l-62),yy+4);} if(x0<=0&&x1>=0){const zx=p.l+(0-x0)/(x1-x0)*(p.r-p.l);ctx.strokeStyle='#17212b';ctx.lineWidth=2;ctx.setLineDash([6,4]);ctx.beginPath();ctx.moveTo(zx,p.t);ctx.lineTo(zx,p.b);ctx.stroke();ctx.setLineDash([]);} if(y0<=0&&y1>=0){const zy=p.b-(0-y0)/(y1-y0)*(p.b-p.t);ctx.strokeStyle='#17212b';ctx.lineWidth=2;ctx.beginPath();ctx.moveTo(p.l,zy);ctx.lineTo(p.r,zy);ctx.stroke();ctx.fillStyle='#17212b';ctx.font='bold 13px system-ui';ctx.fillText('0',p.l-15,zy+4);ctx.font='12px system-ui';} }
